quests.hint: MAKING CONTACT WITH SOMEONE, OFTEN USED AS A POLITE WAY TO OPEN A BUSINESS EMAIL
quests.explanation: REACH OUT is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to make contact, very common in professional email openings. THROUGH, AWAY, and ALONG don't form this specific fixed expression.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes this email opener.
wrongCollocations: reach through to a colleague
reach along to a client
quests.contextSentence: I wanted to reach ___ regarding the proposal you sent last week.

quests.hint: CHECKING IN ABOUT SOMETHING THAT WAS ALREADY DISCUSSED, RATHER THAN COMPLETING A PROMISE YOU MADE
quests.explanation: FOLLOW UP fits here because the email is about checking in on a past conversation. FOLLOW THROUGH is a different fixed phrase meaning to complete a commitment, which doesn't match this specific context about revisiting a discussion.
quests.instruction: Read the context, then choose the word that fits this email situation.
wrongCollocations: follow through on last week's chat
follow around the conversation topic
quests.contextSentence: I'm writing to follow ___ on our conversation from last week about the contract renewal.

quests.hint: A FILE THAT'S LINKED DIRECTLY TO AN EMAIL, RATHER THAN INCLUDED WITH A PHYSICAL LETTER
quests.explanation: PLEASE FIND ATTACHED is correct for digital emails with a file attachment. ENCLOSED is used specifically for physical mail, where an item is placed inside an envelope — a common mix-up for English learners.
quests.instruction: Read the context, then choose the word for this digital communication.
wrongCollocations: please find enclosed the PDF file
please find included the digital document
quests.contextSentence: Please find ___ the revised budget spreadsheet for your review.

quests.hint: MAKING BRIEF CONTACT WITH SOMEONE TO CHECK IN, OFTEN USED CASUALLY AT WORK
quests.explanation: TOUCH BASE is a fixed idiom meaning to make brief contact to check in. GROUND, POINT, and CONTACT don't complete this specific fixed workplace expression.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes this meeting phrase.
wrongCollocations: touch ground with the team
touch point before the deadline
quests.contextSentence: Let's touch ___ again on Thursday to see how the project is going.

quests.hint: RETURNING TO A TOPIC LATER, AFTER MOVING ON TO SOMETHING ELSE FIRST
quests.explanation: CIRCLE BACK is a fixed idiom, common in modern business meetings, meaning to revisit a topic later. AROUND, FORWARD, and OVER don't complete this specific fixed expression.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this meeting phrase.
wrongCollocations: circle around to that topic
circle forward to the budget question
quests.contextSentence: Let's circle ___ to the budget question once we've covered the agenda.

quests.hint: FORMALLY PUTTING FORWARD A PROPOSAL FOR THE GROUP TO VOTE ON OR DISCUSS
quests.explanation: TABLE A MOTION is the classic fixed phrase from formal meeting procedure. SUGGESTION, IDEA, and THOUGHT don't form this specific formal parliamentary expression.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this formal meeting phrase.
wrongCollocations: table a suggestion for discussion
table a thought before the vote
quests.contextSentence: The committee chair tabled a ___ to postpone the vote until next month.

quests.hint: MAKING SURE READERS NOTICE AN IMPORTANT DETAIL IN A REPORT
quests.explanation: DRAW ATTENTION TO is a fixed phrase for pointing out something important in writing. FOCUS, REGARD, and EMPHASIS don't complete this specific fixed expression the same way.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes this report phrase.
wrongCollocations: draw focus to the anomaly
draw emphasis to page twelve
quests.contextSentence: The auditors wanted to draw ___ to an unusual pattern in the quarterly spending.

quests.hint: POINTING OUT A DIFFERENCE BETWEEN TWO SETS OF NUMBERS THAT SHOULD HAVE MATCHED
quests.explanation: HIGHLIGHT A DISCREPANCY is standard report language for pointing out a mismatch. SIMILARITY, AGREEMENT, and CONSISTENCY describe the opposite — figures that match rather than differ.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this report finding.
wrongCollocations: highlight a similarity between matching figures
highlight the consistency in the two reports
quests.contextSentence: The report highlighted a significant ___ between the projected and actual costs.

quests.hint: LAYING OUT SPECIFIC, ACTIONABLE STEPS FOR IMPROVEMENT, RATHER THAN JUST DESCRIBING WHAT WAS DISCOVERED
quests.explanation: OUTLINE RECOMMENDATIONS fits here because the sentence specifically asks for concrete actions for improvement. FINDINGS, RESULTS, and CONCLUSIONS describe what was discovered, not the suggested next steps the context calls for.
quests.instruction: Read the context, then choose the word that fits this report section.
wrongCollocations: outline the findings for improving retention
outline the results for the next quarter
quests.contextSentence: The final section will outline concrete ___ for improving customer retention.

quests.hint: SHIFTING THE FOCUS OF A TALK TO A NEW TOPIC IN A SMOOTH, FORMAL WAY
quests.explanation: TURN OUR ATTENTION TO is a fixed transition phrase used in formal presentations. EYES, WORDS, and THOUGHTS don't complete this specific fixed expression the same way.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes this presentation transition.
wrongCollocations: turn our eyes to the next slide
turn our words to the budget
quests.contextSentence: Let's now turn our ___ to the second half of the proposal.

quests.hint: BRINGING A PRESENTATION OR MEETING TO A CLOSE
quests.explanation: WRAP UP is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to conclude something. DOWN, OVER, and AROUND don't complete this specific fixed expression about ending a talk.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this closing phrase.
wrongCollocations: wrap down the presentation
wrap around the meeting
quests.contextSentence: To wrap ___, I'd like to summarize the three key takeaways from today's talk.

quests.hint: OPENING THE FLOOR SO THE AUDIENCE CAN ASK THINGS AFTER A TALK
quests.explanation: TAKE QUESTIONS is the standard fixed phrase for inviting an audience to ask things. ANSWERS, RESPONSES, and REPLIES don't fit this specific phrase, since a speaker takes questions but doesn't 'take' the responses themselves.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this presentation phrase.
wrongCollocations: take a few answers before continuing
take some replies from the audience
quests.contextSentence: I'll take a few ___ before we move on to the next section.

quests.hint: PEOPLE WHO PROVIDED INFORMATION FOR A NEWS STORY BUT WEREN'T NAMED, ESPECIALLY WHEN CLOSELY CONNECTED TO AN INVESTIGATION
quests.explanation: ACCORDING TO SOURCES fits because journalism specifically uses the phrase 'sources close to' an investigation. WITNESSES, REPORTERS, and OFFICIALS don't fit this exact fixed journalistic expression about unnamed informants.
quests.instruction: Read the context, then choose the word that fits this news phrase.
wrongCollocations: according to witnesses close to the investigation
according to reporters close to the investigation
quests.contextSentence: According to ___ close to the investigation, an arrest is expected within days.

quests.hint: GIVING INFORMATION TO A JOURNALIST WITHOUT LETTING YOUR NAME BE PUBLISHED
quests.explanation: SPEAKING ON CONDITION OF ANONYMITY is the fixed journalistic phrase for an unnamed source. SECRECY, PRIVACY, and CONFIDENTIALITY are related in meaning but don't form this specific fixed expression used in news writing.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this journalistic phrase.
wrongCollocations: speaking on condition of secrecy
speaking on condition of privacy
quests.contextSentence: A senior official, speaking on condition of ___, confirmed the details of the plan.

quests.hint: REFUSING TO GIVE A STATEMENT TO A JOURNALIST, AS OFTEN QUOTED WORD FOR WORD IN NEWS ARTICLES
quests.explanation: DECLINED TO COMMENT is the standard fixed phrase quoted in news articles when someone refuses to speak to the press. RESPOND, ANSWER, and REPLY are grammatically possible, but COMMENT is overwhelmingly the expected word in this exact journalistic formula.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this news phrase.
wrongCollocations: declined to respond to journalists
declined to reply to the press
quests.contextSentence: The company spokesperson declined to ___ when asked about the layoffs.

quests.hint: SAYING SOMETHING AFTER A LONG, AWKWARD PAUSE IN A CONVERSATION
quests.explanation: BREAK THE SILENCE is a fixed idiom for finally speaking after a long pause. QUIET, STILLNESS, and CALM don't form this specific fixed expression, even though they relate to silence.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes this conversational moment.
wrongCollocations: break the quiet at the dinner table
break the calm after the argument
quests.contextSentence: After a long, awkward pause, he finally broke the ___.

quests.hint: SWITCHING WHAT YOU'RE TALKING ABOUT, OFTEN BECAUSE THE CURRENT TOPIC FEELS UNCOMFORTABLE
quests.explanation: CHANGE THE SUBJECT is the fixed everyday idiom for switching topics. THEME, MATTER, and POINT don't form this specific fixed conversational expression.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this conversational habit.
wrongCollocations: change the theme when uncomfortable
change the point to avoid the question
quests.contextSentence: Whenever his salary comes up, he quickly changes the ___.

quests.hint: STOPPING SMALL TALK AND MOVING DIRECTLY TO THE MAIN THING YOU WANT TO SAY
quests.explanation: GET TO THE POINT is a fixed everyday idiom for moving directly to what matters. ISSUE, MATTER, and TOPIC don't form this specific fixed conversational expression.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this conversational request.
wrongCollocations: get to the issue quickly
get to the topic without delay
quests.contextSentence: Stop rambling and just get to the ___ already.

quests.hint: BEING NOTICEABLY DIFFERENT FROM EVERYONE ELSE COMPETING FOR THE SAME JOB, IN A GOOD WAY
quests.explanation: STAND OUT FROM THE CROWD is a fixed idiom for being noticeably better than the competition. GROUP, HERD, and POOL don't form this specific fixed expression, even though they relate to a collection of people.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes this career idiom.
wrongCollocations: stand out from the group of candidates
stand out from the pool of applicants
quests.contextSentence: A well-written cover letter can help your application stand out from the ___.

quests.hint: HAVING THE SPECIFIC QUALIFICATIONS A JOB LISTING SAYS YOU NEED BEFORE APPLYING
quests.explanation: MEET THE REQUIREMENTS fits because the context specifically mentions qualifications listed in a job posting. CRITERIA, QUALIFICATIONS, and SPECIFICATIONS are close synonyms, but REQUIREMENTS is the everyday standard word used in this exact context.
quests.instruction: Read the context, then choose the word that fits.
wrongCollocations: meet the criteria in the listing
meet the specifications in the posting
quests.contextSentence: Before applying, make sure you meet the minimum ___ listed in the posting, such as three years of experience.

quests.hint: MAILING A SHORT MESSAGE OF APPRECIATION AFTER A JOB INTERVIEW
quests.explanation: SEND A THANK-YOU is the standard fixed phrase for this post-interview courtesy. GRATITUDE, APPRECIATION, and ACKNOWLEDGMENT are abstract nouns that don't pair naturally with SEND the way the concrete compound THANK-YOU does.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this career-advice phrase.
wrongCollocations: send gratitude after the interview
send appreciation to the interviewer
quests.contextSentence: Career coaches always recommend you send a ___ note within 24 hours of the interview.

quests.hint: SAYING SORRY FOR A DISRUPTION CAUSED TO A CUSTOMER, IN THE STANDARD PHRASE COMPANIES USE
quests.explanation: APOLOGIZE FOR THE INCONVENIENCE is the standard fixed customer-service phrase. TROUBLE, DISRUPTION, and DIFFICULTY are close synonyms, but INCONVENIENCE is overwhelmingly the expected word in formal corporate apologies.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes this customer-service phrase.
wrongCollocations: apologize for the trouble in formal letters
apologize for the difficulty caused
quests.contextSentence: We sincerely apologize for the ___ this delay may have caused.

quests.hint: SETTLING A CUSTOMER'S COMPLAINT, DESCRIBED IN THE FORMAL, SOMEWHAT VAGUE LANGUAGE COMPANIES OFTEN USE FOR A PROBLEM
quests.explanation: RESOLVE THE MATTER fits the formal, slightly vague register typical of corporate customer-service language, where 'matter' stands in for the complaint itself. APPOINTMENT, INVOICE, and SCHEDULE are unrelated business nouns that don't describe an unresolved complaint at all.
quests.instruction: Read the context, then choose the word that fits this formal tone.
wrongCollocations: resolve the appointment as quickly as possible
resolve the invoice caused by the delay
quests.contextSentence: We assure you that we are doing everything possible to resolve this ___ as quickly as possible.

quests.hint: PROVIDING MONEY BACK TO A CUSTOMER AS A GESTURE OF GOODWILL, THE MOST STANDARD REMEDY MENTIONED IN APOLOGIES
quests.explanation: OFFER A REFUND is the standard fixed customer-service remedy phrase. REPLACEMENT, EXCHANGE, and CREDIT are other possible remedies, but REFUND is the most standard and expected word in this general apology context.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this customer-service gesture.
wrongCollocations: offer a replacement as the only remedy
offer a credit instead of money
quests.contextSentence: As a gesture of goodwill, we would like to offer you a full ___ for the inconvenience caused.

quests.hint: ARGUING THE OPPOSITE SIDE OF A DEBATE JUST TO TEST HOW STRONG AN ARGUMENT REALLY IS
quests.explanation: PLAY DEVIL'S ADVOCATE is a fixed idiom for arguing an opposing view to test an argument's strength, common in academic discussions. LAWYER, DEFENDER, and SUPPORTER don't complete this specific fixed idiomatic expression.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes this academic idiom.
wrongCollocations: play devil's lawyer in the seminar
play devil's supporter during class
quests.contextSentence: Just to play devil's ___, what if the study's sample size was too small?

quests.hint: PRESENTING AN ALTERNATIVE PERSPECTIVE THAT CHALLENGES SOMEONE'S CLAIM, RATHER THAN SIMPLY CRITICIZING IT
quests.explanation: RAISE A COUNTERPOINT fits because the context describes offering an alternative view rather than a harsh criticism. OBJECTION, REBUTTAL, and CRITICISM imply a more negative or confrontational tone than the constructive academic exchange described here.
quests.instruction: Read the context, then choose the word that fits this academic exchange.
wrongCollocations: raise an objection harshly in class
raise a criticism aggressively during discussion
quests.contextSentence: To challenge the professor's claim, she raised an interesting ___ based on last week's reading.

quests.hint: POLITELY STATING THAT YOU HOLD A DIFFERENT VIEW, WITHOUT BEING RUDE ABOUT IT
quests.explanation: RESPECTFULLY DISAGREE is the standard fixed polite academic phrase. OBJECT, PROTEST, and ARGUE don't combine as naturally with RESPECTFULLY, which specifically softens the act of disagreeing.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this polite academic phrase.
wrongCollocations: respectfully object during the seminar
respectfully protest the professor's claim
quests.contextSentence: I would have to respectfully ___ with the conclusion drawn in this paper.

quests.hint: GIVING YOUR SUPPORT TO SOMEONE WITH GREAT ENTHUSIASM, USING THE MOST COMMON WORD FOR THIS IN REFERENCE LETTERS
quests.explanation: HIGHLY RECOMMEND is the most common phrase used in reference letters for enthusiastic endorsement. DEEPLY, INTENSELY, and POWERFULLY don't combine as naturally with RECOMMEND in this specific formal context.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes this reference-letter phrase.
wrongCollocations: deeply recommend a candidate in letters
intensely recommend an employee formally
quests.contextSentence: I ___ recommend her for this position without any reservations.

quests.hint: GIVING YOUR SUPPORT COMPLETELY AND CONFIDENTLY, WITH NO UNCERTAINTY AT ALL
quests.explanation: RECOMMEND WITHOUT HESITATION is the standard fixed phrase in professional recommendation letters. DOUBT, QUESTION, and PAUSE are related in meaning but don't form this specific fixed formal expression.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this reference-letter phrase.
wrongCollocations: recommend without doubt in formal letters
recommend without question to employers
quests.contextSentence: I can recommend him without any ___ for this leadership role.

quests.hint: DESCRIBING SOMEONE APPLYING FOR A JOB WHO IS EXCEPTIONALLY QUALIFIED, IN THE STANDARD LANGUAGE OF REFERENCE LETTERS
quests.explanation: OUTSTANDING CANDIDATE is the standard phrase in professional recommendation letters. APPLICANT, CONTESTANT, and NOMINEE are related terms, but CANDIDATE is the word most consistently used in this specific formal context.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this reference-letter phrase.
wrongCollocations: outstanding applicant in a casual note
outstanding nominee for the position
quests.contextSentence: In my ten years of hiring, she remains one of the most ___ candidates I've encountered.
